## Appeal Letter

Dear Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield,

I am writing to appeal the out-of-network penalty applied to claim #CLM-2024-02387 for emergency services rendered on January 5, 2024 at Riverside General Hospital. [S1]

Under the No Surprises Act (effective January 1, 2022), patients are protected from out-of-network cost-sharing for emergency services, regardless of whether the facility is in-network. [S2]

The services rendered constituted emergency care as defined under 42 U.S.C. §300gg-111(a)(3)(C). The patient presented with acute chest pain and was admitted via the emergency department. [S3]

We request that this claim be reprocessed at the in-network rate.

Sincerely,
David Park

summary.explanation: You were charged out-of-network rates for emergency care at a hospital outside your plan's network. The No Surprises Act (2022) generally prohibits insurers from applying out-of-network cost-sharing for emergency services. This is a strong protection — your insurer is required by federal law to treat emergency care as in-network.

rule_sources.text: A health plan shall not impose a cost-sharing requirement greater than the cost-sharing requirement that would apply for in-network emergency services.

success_estimate.explanation: The No Surprises Act is a strong federal protection for emergency care. However, the insurer may contest the emergency classification. The outcome depends on whether the admission records clearly document an emergent condition.

## Appeal Letter

Dear Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield,

I am writing to appeal the out-of-network penalty applied to claim #CLM-2024-02387 for emergency services rendered on January 5, 2024 at Riverside General Hospital. [S1]

Under the No Surprises Act (effective January 1, 2022), patients are protected from out-of-network cost-sharing for emergency services, regardless of whether the facility is in-network. [S2]

The services rendered constituted emergency care as defined under 42 U.S.C. §300gg-111(a)(3)(C). The patient presented with acute chest pain and was admitted via the emergency department. [S3]

We request that this claim be reprocessed at the in-network rate.

Sincerely,
David Park

S1.text: Out-of-network services are subject to separate deductibles and coinsurance. Emergency services are exempt as required by applicable law.

S2.text: A health plan shall not impose a cost-sharing requirement greater than the cost-sharing requirement that would apply for in-network emergency services.

S3.text: Emergency medical condition means a medical condition manifesting itself by acute symptoms of sufficient severity such that the absence of immediate medical attention could reasonably be expected to result in placing the patient in serious jeopardy.
